nca3eac692978: Many jurisdictions have sought to mitigate hurdles faced by people with criminal records by allowing those records to be expunged (or sealed). Expungement eliminates most legal restrictions triggered by records, and policymakers hope it could also improve access to employment and housing markets and reduce social stigma. Yet there remain significant questions about how well this intervention works. This article canvasses the nascent empirical literature on expungement, focusing on three areas. First, uptake studies consistently find that when eligible individuals must file legal petitions for expungement, only a small fraction do so. Second, studies of those who do receive petition-based expungement have mostly found positive effects on employment and other outcomes. However, the uptake problem introduces sample selection concerns that complicate causal inference, and one recent randomized control trial found a disappointing absence of effects. Third, research on automated expungement (carried out by the state without individuals petitioning) is especially limited, but there is some reason for skepticism about its effects, at least on employment.
nc0b7b171a689: This review centers on the development of labeling theory in criminology. Our core argument is that modifications to labeling theory in the past several decades have veered research away from the theory's core propositions. We extend this argument by presenting a three-part conceptual model of secondary deviance, defined as persistence in deviant behavior as a result of punishment. First, a subtheory of punishment and social exclusion explains institutional and interpersonal exclusion after punishment as the result of selection, separation, and stigma. Stigma manifests as rejection, withdrawal, and homophily. Second, deviant identity is reintroduced as the central motivating mechanism of secondary deviance. Its development involves the links between actual and reflected appraisals and the internalization of reflected appraisals into self-appraisals. Third, peer and community contexts are sources of variation in the effects of punishment on social exclusion and deviant identity. Researchers should give special attention to how these processes unfold within individuals and across life stages. Our model serves as a framework for advancing understanding of the mechanisms that drive criminogenic consequences of punishment.
nfe6d350af04f: Police violence remains pervasive across democratic societies in the Americas. This review brings the US literature on policing into dialogue with comparative research on Latin America to identify common forces that sustain what we call punitive policing—systems of law enforcement that systematically violate human rights, rely on excessive surveillance and coercion, and disproportionately target marginalized populations. Synthesizing scholarship from both regions, the review highlights three factors that help explain the persistence of punitive policing: colonial legacies, the militarization of public security, and deeply entrenched racial and socioeconomic inequalities that shape how police are deployed and whom they target with violence. Our review shows that punitive policing is a governance problem that undermines legitimacy, public safety, citizenship, and democratic stability. Yet the evidence also suggests that meaningful reform is possible when bottom-up, coordinated mobilization converges with top-down institutional intervention to constrain punitive policing.
n2712d9bba975: Scholars of mass incarceration have tended to understand the prison as a labor market institution mostly in the negative sense: as a warehouse for those otherwise likely to be unemployed and as a site of status degradation that further reduces people's ability to find employment after release. In this article, we review recent work that has focused attention on the prison as a labor market institution in a more productive sense: as an organization that shapes the work activity of the many workers incarcerated within it, facilitates formerly incarcerated people's subordination in the labor market upon release, and may play a more active role than previously imagined in shaping the distribution of jobs available in the US labor market as a whole. We also introduce new evidence that the tightness of the labor market structures how a criminal record shapes people's labor market experiences after incarceration.
n19158c5f9c67: Fish schools are among the most spectacular examples of collective behavior in nature. Individual fish coordinate their motion with neighbors primarily through vision and flow sensing. Each fish generates flow disturbances that can influence the motion and energetics of nearby swimmers. Yet fundamental questions remain unresolved: To what extent can schooling be explained by passive hydrodynamic interactions, and where are individual-level sensing and control required to maintain group cohesion? This review examines collective swimming through the lens of fluid mechanics. By synthesizing experimental, theoretical, and computational studies spanning pairs of fish to large schools, I discuss how hydrodynamic interactions affect coordination, stability, and energetic cost. Flow interactions can yield robust pairwise coordination and locomotor benefits, but they can also drive collective instabilities and unequal benefit distributions in larger groups. These findings point to a fundamental interplay between hydrodynamics and sensory–motor feedback in the formation and maintenance of fish schools. More broadly, they suggest that hydrodynamics shapes collective swimming not only through energetic costs and benefits but also through the physical constraints it imposes on coordination, stability, and information flow within groups.
nd37b0c5a9cba: Cell identity is established by tightly regulated transcriptional programs. Disruption of the regulatory mechanisms governing these programs leads to aberrant behavior and, frequently, cancer. Enhancer hijacking, the process whereby a gene comes under the control of an ectopic enhancer, is a major cause of transcriptional dysregulation. Although recognized since the 1980s, its detection has been traditionally hindered by the low resolution of karyotyping and incomplete knowledge of enhancer biology. This has changed with the development of high-throughput sequencing, leading to a surge in newly identified enhancer hijacking events over the past two decades. Furthermore, functional dissection of enhancers using techniques such as CRISPR/Cas9 has shed light on their mechanistic underpinnings, with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) emerging as a paradigm for this phenomenon. In this review, we outline the historical development of enhancer hijacking, highlight representative examples in hematological malignancies, and discuss the insights derived from this research, particularly in AML.
ne665ba23399c: Circadian rhythms organize mammalian physiology across the 24-h day through molecular clocks coordinated by the central clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus and distributed to peripheral oscillators. These clocks regulate processes central to pharmacology, including drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, elimination, and target responsiveness. Consequently, drug efficacy and toxicity can vary substantially depending on the time of administration. Despite decades of progress in pharmacogenomics and systems pharmacology, consideration of time of day remains largely absent from clinical drug development and prescription. In this review, we evaluate emerging research on circadian regulation of drug responses, considering both pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. We review chronotherapeutic strategies to treat diseases, including cancer, cardiovascular disease, and bipolar disorder. We also discuss the use of wearable technologies to enable time-resolved drug evaluation. Finally, we discuss the challenges to clinical translation and the integration of circadian timing into precision medicine and optimized dosing strategies.
ne54f6e1de336: The endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling system is a local regulator of synaptic activity across brain circuits involved in the regulation of emotional behaviors. Preclinical studies predominantly show that eCB signaling dampens acute stress responses, although notable exceptions exist. Various forms of chronic stress downregulate eCB signaling, and enhanced eCB tone can reduce the effects of chronic stress on avoidance behaviors and anhedonia. Studies in healthy humans generally align with these preclinical findings. Type 1 cannabinoid receptors (CB1Rs) and fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), the enzyme that degrades the eCB N -arachidonoylethanolamine (AEA), are present in circuits that regulate emotion, and pharmacological and genetic manipulations of these proteins affect anxiety, stress responses, and reward. However, FAAH inhibitors have largely failed to demonstrate efficacy, and CB1R agonists have only modest effects in individuals with mood disorders. Advancing the therapeutic potential of CB1R/eCB signaling likely will require a deeper understanding of the factors contributing to inconsistencies between model systems and individuals with mood disorders.
n22c20b60d1b2: Exercise delivers a wide variety of health benefits through many mechanisms, including the release of exerkines, signaling molecules secreted by multiple tissues during physical activity. We evaluated 34 exerkines with therapeutic potential alongside IC7Fc (an engineered IL-6/CNTF derivative), classifying them based on ( a ) their translational readiness as therapeutics and ( b ) their primary clinical domains (cardiovascular, metabolic, neurological, musculoskeletal, anti-inflammatory, and oncology). Only four have clear clinical validation, and nine others have reached clinical testing or late preclinical development. Across these molecular entities, three challenges emerge: context-dependent effects, drug-delivery constraints, and network dynamics. We conclude with an assessment of opportunities and strategies for the creation of exerkine-based biomarkers and for using exerkines to facilitate therapeutic discovery. Finally, we present the Exerkine Atlas ( https://exerkineatlas.org/ ), an open-access web resource integrating curated literature and clinical trial data for all 35 molecules.
ne71424676c7d: Cannabis and tobacco are two of the most commonly used drugs worldwide. Both drugs can lead to a use disorder, characterized by compulsive use despite harm and mediated by neurobiological changes in reward and motivational circuitry. Co-use of cannabis and tobacco is common and influences disorder severity and outcomes. Both cannabis use disorder (CUD) and tobacco use disorder (TUD) share key features, such as dopaminergic reward system involvement, severity of withdrawal symptoms, and mental health comorbidities, yet they differ in neurobiological pathways, diagnostic profiles, and available pharmacotherapies. Diagnostic frameworks like the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, and International Classification of Diseases 11 provide standardized criteria for assessment. Optimal management integrates pharmacological and psychosocial interventions, though approved medications exist for TUD and not yet for CUD. Understanding similarities, distinctions, and treatment strategies is critical for effective prevention and clinical care.
n55c24fe66b3f: Missing data is a challenging issue in data analysis. Researchers often address the issue by simply removing incomplete cases from the analysis. However, this approach reduces the sample size and can undermine the accuracy of statistical estimates. Alternatively, imputation techniques can be used to replace missing values with plausible estimates, resulting in a more complete dataset and more reliable estimates. In this study, we propose a new imputation method, which we call Layered Stacking. The method is designed to improve the estimation of continuous missing values. To evaluate its effectiveness, comprehensive simulation studies were carried out with four distinct data generating processes using datasets generated under the missing at random mechanism, with sample sizes of 500, 1,000, 5,000 and 10,000, and missingness rates of 10, 20, 30 and 40%. The proposed method is compared with five widely used imputation techniques: k-nearest neighbors, support vector regression, decision tree, random forest and extreme gradient boosting. Evaluation metrics include mean squared imputation error (MSIE) and mean absolute percentage imputation error (MAPIE) along with standard deviation (SD) and 95% confidence interval (CI) across replications. Two real-world datasets have also been considered to assess the performance of the method. The proposed method generally achieved lower MSIE than the benchmark models, particularly for larger datasets.
n54d45d29b640: Background There is a growing imperative for nurses to navigate multicultural healthcare systems and deliver quality, responsive, safe, person-centred care. Accordingly, undergraduate nursing education must be relevant and innovative to provide undergraduate nursing students with meaningful learning opportunities to develop cultural competence. This study aims to assess undergraduate nursing students’ cultural awareness and examine how these perceptions vary according to socio-demographic characteristics. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted utilising a valid and standardised tool, the cultural awareness scale (CAS). “One hundred and sixteen” undergraduate nursing students from a higher education institution participated in the study. The Mann–Whitney U test and the Kruskal–Wallis test were used to examine differences in CAS scores across subscales and total scores according to participants’ socio-demographic characteristics. Results Overall, the CAS results showed students’ level of cultural awareness was moderately high, with slight variations across the four CAS subscales. Participants born in Ireland had higher scores on all subscales compared to participants born outside Ireland, although these differences were not statistically significant. Participants who identified as White scored highest on General Education Experience (64.54 vs 42.66, U = 837, p = 0.002, r = −0.29), and Total Awareness (63.32 vs 45.86, U = 939.5, p = 0.012, r = −0.23) compared with participants who were categorised as people of colour. Conclusions The cultural awareness scores in this study were moderately high among undergraduate nursing students, consistent with previous research using the CAS instrument. The findings suggest an association between ethnic background and perceptions of culturally inclusive educational practices and highlight the need for further research to explore these patterns and inform the development of culturally responsive nursing education.
nb6faf5eafd06: by Sarah M. Faisal, Samer Imad Mohammed Background Kidney transplant care in low-resource countries is often affected by multiple factors, including workforce constraints, fragmented communication, and medication access challenges. Given pharmacists’ involvement in medication management and regular patient follow-up, this study was designed to explore transplant care delivery in Iraq from pharmacists’ perspectives. Method Qualitative data were collected using face-to-face, semi-structured interviews with all eligible pharmacists from the two major governmental hospitals in Baghdad caring for kidney transplant recipients. Afterwards, data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis approach. Results This study included 13 pharmacists, 5 of whom were working in the clinical transplant wards, whereas the remaining 8 were working in the outpatient consultation setting. Four descriptive themes were identified: Dispensing-centered practice within a constrained and evolving pharmacist role, fragmented yet adaptive interprofessional collaboration, patient education as an informal and inconsistently delivered practice, and medication availability within a constrained and variably regulated supply system. Conclusion This study highlights the adaptive approaches used by pharmacists in an attempt to maintain medication access and patient support with the available resources. However, the study findings also highlight challenges that extend beyond the capacity of individual pharmacists to resolve and suggest the need for more structured organizational support, clearer communication pathways, and an integrated system to strengthen Iraqi transplant care practices within comparable governmental settings.
na3c16749b660: Several animal groups produce two morphologically distinct types of sperm in the testis, including fertilizing eusperm and non-fertilizing parasperm. This phenomenon, termed sperm dimorphism, is considered to play a role in reproductive strategies such as sperm competition. In the marine gastropod Conomurex luhuanus, parasperm possess numerous globular bodies and the cilia-based undulating membranes. However, the function of the globular bodies and the motility of the undulating membranes remain unclear. Here, we describe the process and regulation of globular body exocytosis in parasperm. Upon dilution in artificial seawater, exocytosis occurs via membrane fusion between globular body membrane and the plasma membrane, followed by the release of globular body contents. Exocytosis was markedly suppressed under Ca2+ -deficient conditions but was enhanced by increases in intracellular Ca2+ induced by an ionophore A23187. In contrast, both the absence of extracellular K⁺ and high extracellular K⁺ concentrations enhanced exocytosis. On the other hand, the direction of wave propagation of the undulating membrane was reversed by high extracellular Ca2+ concentrations or by treatment with A23187, whereas it was suppressed under high extracellular K⁺ conditions. Together, these findings indicate that globular body exocytosis and changes in swimming direction are regulated by different mechanisms. This study provides novel insight into the post-ejaculatory behavior and potential function of parasperm within the female reproductive tract of gastropods.
n760268eb4b2e: by Tracy M. Stewart, Gillean McCluskey, Hamish Johnson, Debi Fry, Lesley McAra, Josie N. Booth Addressing the mental health needs of children and young people requires integrated and multidisciplinary action to reduce the risk of detrimental outcomes. Schools offer a unique environment for such provision. However, there is a critical need for school-based interventions that are feasible, co-designed, transdiagnostic, sustainable, and cost-effective beyond the conclusion of the trial, while aligning with pupil and teacher preferences. The current study reports the development phase of a new school-based transdiagnostic mental health intervention, embedded into routine classroom lessons, which aims to promote mental health and prevent the onset or escalation of mental health symptoms in young people. The study involved a total of 32 participants aged 15–63 years (Mage = 32.72, SD = 12.73), across three groups: one group of teachers (Mage = 36.80, SD = 11.29) took part in four sequential development workshops, one group of young people (Mage = 15.85, SD = 0.69) took part in one development workshop, and a new group of teachers who were not part of the initial development took part in one refinement workshop (Mage = 37.38, SD = 9.26). The study identified mental health priority areas in the classroom and brought together teachers and young people to co-develop activities that can be integrated directly into routine teaching to support and promote mental health. The intervention was deemed feasible and acceptable by both teachers and young people, subject to contextual considerations. Teachers perceived the activities to have a positive impact on young people’s mental health, engagement, learning, energy, and overall enjoyment in class. The development of this intervention, with its co-production approach, has the potential to bridge the gap in intervention translation to the classroom and ultimately benefit young people’s mental health.
ne6517e1d1634: by Patricia Kreis, Rita Hendricusdottir, Louise Kay, Ismini E. Papageorgiou, Michiel van Diepen, Till Mack, Jonny Ryves, Adrian Harwood, Nicholas R. Leslie, Oliver Kann, Maddy Parsons, Britta J. Eickholt
n96ba3a88be29: This study aimed to develop a one-step loop-mediated isothermal amplification combined with a lateral flow dipstick (LAMP-LFD) DNA biosensor for the detection of α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion). Genomic DNA was obtained from 48 α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion)-positive and 48 (SEA deletion)-negative (normal) Thai subjects. DNA was analyzed by LAMP assay at 61°C for 60 min using specific primers for the α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion) type. Following amplification, the products were visually detected using an LFD, with results available within 5–10 min. The one-step LAMP-LFD DNA biosensor could detect DNA carrying the α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion) type at levels as low as 200 pg, with 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity. Furthermore, no cross-reactivity was observed with DNA carrying other α0-thalassemia deletion types (THAI deletion). The LAMP-LFD DNA biosensor is useful for identifying carriers of α0-thalassemia (SEA deletion) (the most common deletion type found in Thailand and across Southeast Asia). This novel one-step LAMP-LFD kit will be beneficial for medical laboratory technologists performing genetic carrier screening tests as it is simple to perform and requires minimal equipment and time. Furthermore, this method supports clinicians in providing genetic counseling and implementing preventive strategies against severe thalassemia, a significant public health concern in Thailand.
n8bb4a3a96dd5: Optimal nutrition is a central to the care of people receiving maintenance hemodialysis, yet dietary intake in these patients is usually measured by self-report, and self-report is known to be unreliable. Evidence from resource-limited dialysis settings is scarce. This cross-sectional study assessed dietary intake among 181 adults receiving maintenance hemodialysis at four hospital-based units in Bangladesh, and examined how screening reported intake for plausibility changes conclusions about guideline adherence. Intake was measured by three non-consecutive 24-hour recalls and compared with the Kidney Disease Outcomes Quality Initiative (KDOQI) recommendations. Reporting plausibility was classified from the ratio of energy intake to estimated basal metabolic rate. Appetite was assessed using the Appetite and Diet Assessment Tool. Of 178 participants with complete data, 65.2% reported acceptable, 32.0% under-reported and 2.8% over-reported energy intake. In the cohort as a whole, only 20 of 176 (11.4%) met the energy target of 30–35 kcal/kg/day and 58 (33.0%) met the protein target of at least 1.0 g/kg/day. Screening changed these estimates in opposite directions according to the type of target. For intake targets, adherence rose once implausible reports were excluded: energy from 11.4% to 15.5% and protein from 33.0% to 47.4%. For restriction targets the reverse occurred: apparent adherence to the sodium limit fell from 73.6% to 65.5% and to the phosphorus limit from 88.2% to 84.5%. The phosphorus-to-protein ratio exceeded 12 mg/g in all but five participants. Poor appetite was common (42.0%) but did not correspond to lower measured intake, and was instead associated with reporting plausibility (p = 0.024). Unscreened self-reported intake simultaneously overstates dietary inadequacy and understates dietary excess, and should not be used unfiltered to guide nutritional decisions in this population.
n059c04579f5a: Background Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a common complication of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and a leading cause of end-stage renal disease, posing substantial health and economic burdens. Early self-management interventions targeting modifiable risk factors are crucial to prevent or slow DKD progression. However, most studies focus on later stages of DKD, leaving a gap in early prevention for high risk of DKD individuals. Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of a structured self-management intervention on clinical outcomes among T2DM patients at high risk of DKD. Design A prospective, two-arm, randomized controlled trial. Setting A tertiary hospital in Shandong Province, China. Participants 134 patients with T2DM who were classified as being at high risk of DKD using a validated DKD risk prediction model. Methods 134 participants were randomized 1:1 to the intervention or control group. The intervention group received a 12-week a structured self-management program and 12-week follow-up. The control group received usual care. Clinical outcomes included hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), systolic blood pressure (SBP), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC) were collected at baseline (T0), after the 12-week intervention (T1), and at 24 weeks (T2). Generalized estimating equations and intention-to-treat analyses were performed. Sensitivity analyses using multiple imputation were conducted. Results All participants completed the intervention phase. During the follow-up visits period, 7 participants in the intervention group and 9 participants in the control group were lost to follow-up at T1 (attrition rate: 11.94%), while 5 participants in the intervention group and 4 participants in the control group were lost to follow-up at T2 (attrition rate: 6.71%). No significant differences in baseline sociodemographic or clinical indicators between participants retained and those lost to follow-up (p > 0.05), suggesting data were missing at random. Baseline comparisons between the intervention and control groups revealed no significant differences in demographic or clinical indicators (p > 0.05). Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated significant improvements in HbA1c, eGFR, SBP, and LDL-C, while no significant differences were observed for UACR, BMI, or WC. Sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. Conclusions The self-management intervention effectively improved HbA1c, eGFR, SBP and LDL-C among T2DM patients at high risk of DKD. These findings suggest that integrating structured self-management into routine diabetes care may help improve modifiable risk factors and support early DKD prevention. Registration China Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400092745; registered on 22 November 2024)
n3ab8bc32295c: Background Mental health problems lead to the loss of about 12 billion workdays worldwide each year. This creates a major economic burden. In food manufacturing, workers often face various psychosocial stressors. These include high workload, time constraint, repetitive tasks, and low autonomy. These conditions can affect both mental health and work performance. Workplace mental health interventions have shown promising results in mental health improvement. However, most studies come from high-income countries and service sectors. There is still limited evidence from industrial settings in middle-income countries. To address this gap, a structured Worksite Mental Health Program (WMHP) was developed. Method This study will employ a quasi-experimental two arm repeated measures design among workers from food manufacturing factories in Malaysia. The intervention group will receive an eight week WMHP including psychoeducation, mindfulness practices, progressive muscle relaxation, and breathing exercises. The comparison group will continue with routine workplace practices and receive a general mental health information pamphlet. Assessments will be carried out at baseline, one month post intervention, and at three months follow up. Primary outcomes include depression, anxiety, stress, and burnout. Secondary outcomes include job satisfaction, absenteeism, presenteeism, and economic outcomes. Changes over time will be analysed using Generalised Estimating Equations (GEE). A cost–benefit analysis (CBA) will also be conducted to assess economic impact. Anticipated results The program is expected to improve mental health and work performance, while simultaneously reducing absenteeism and presenteeism. The economic evaluation is expected to demonstrate positive productivity gains associated with the program. Conclusion This study will provide evidence on the effectiveness and economic value of a workplace mental health intervention in an industrial setting, informing workplace health strategies in Malaysia and similar contexts. Trial registration Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR): TCTR20241217003
n2976d8cbe732: Introduction Non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are a major public health challenge in the United Kingdom (UK), placing strain on the National Health Service (NHS). While Western medicine dominates NCD care, the use of complementary and alternative medicine (CAM), such as Ayurveda, is increasing. The objective of this study was to explore the experiences and perspectives of Ayurvedic practitioners in the UK regarding the use of Ayurveda for managing NCDs. Methods Seventeen UK-based Ayurvedic practitioners participated in semi-structured qualitative interviews that were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed thematically. Findings Three key themes were identified. First, Ayurvedic practitioners viewed their role as complementary to Western medicine, providing holistic, individualised, and patient-centred care to support NCD management. Second, they faced multiple barriers in the UK, including structural challenges (limited integration, poor institutional support, and restricted patient access) and financial constraints (high treatment costs, lack of NHS coverage, and import regulations). Finally, professional associations played a vital role in providing legal and regulatory guidance, promoting continuous professional development, and supporting research to strengthen evidence and legitimacy. Conclusion Although Ayurvedic practitioners face considerable challenges in the UK, they play a unique role in negotiating legitimacy, professional recognition, and the epistemological challenges of practising within a Western-dominated healthcare system. Professional associations help legitimise and advance their practice, supporting culturally congruent, patient-centred care that complements conventional NCD management. Despite structural barriers, Ayurvedic practitioners have maintained their presence and have navigated a complex, structurally Western-centric healthcare landscape, offering insights into integrative approaches to NCD care.
n2616cd60cf19: Background People with kidney disease who need to transition onto kidney replacement therapy (KRT) face a life-changing diagnosis. This process involves complex decisions about treatment and a high volume of healthcare work. Little work has been done looking at KRT transition through the lens of treatment burden. This study aims to explore how treatment burden evolves during KRT transition in a population recruited from a large nephrology and kidney transplant unit in Glasgow, Scotland. Methods and findings Serial in-depth qualitative interviews were conducted with 30 participants across up to three time points, generating 76 interviews. We used a framework analysis informed by Normalisation Process Theory (NPT), Theory of Patient Capacity (TPC) and Burden of Treatment Theory (BoTT) to explore the interaction between workload, capacity, and the system. Five main themes affecting treatment burden arose: engaging personal and social resources to navigate KRT transition, being able to meet the challenges, preparing to enact the healthcare workload, undertaking KRT transition related workload, and the evolution of burden over time. Conclusion Transitioning onto KRT is a process that entails a high volume of healthcare workload and significant treatment burden. Experiences of treatment burden are influenced by the nature of the work required; the patient’s capacity including physical, psychological, financial and cognitive factors; the capacity of their social network; and the functioning of the healthcare system. Particular focus should be placed on understanding the impact of the healthcare system on experiences of burden, as it represents a potentially modifiable driver of treatment burden that clinicians and healthcare policy-makers can directly influence.
ne914990c4863: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) is a severe male infertility disorder. This study aims to identify immune-related biomarkers for explore immune-related molecular signatures associated with NOA. Here, we integrated transcriptomic data from four independent cohorts (GSE145467, GSE45885, GSE45887, GSE9210) using an integrative pipeline combining differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and consensus-based multi-machine learning to identify an immune-related gene signature associated with NOA. We identified 16 immune-related differentially expressed genes through WGCNA, which were refined into a 12-gene panel—Hub NOA.Sig (CD14, CD19, CMTM2, CXCL16, HSPA1L, HSPA2, IGF1, IL13, POMC, RBP1, STAB2, TYROBP)—using five feature selection algorithms (Bagged Trees, Bayesian, Boruta, LASSO, LVQ). A Random Forest classifier based on Hub NOA.Sig yielded good classification performance with an AUC of 0.87. This signature offers a transcriptomic reference for characterizing NOA heterogeneity and exploring immune-related molecular features. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) revealed significant alterations in six immune cell populations—including effector memory CD4 ⁺ /CD8 ⁺ T cells, regulatory T cells, and plasmacytoid dendritic cells—and demonstrated strong correlations between hub genes and specific immune infiltrates. Furthermore, drug-gene interaction screening and molecular docking predicted loperamide-POMC, acitretin-RBP1, and retinol-RBP1 as candidate drug-gene pairs for subsequent experimental validation. This work provides transcriptomic clues and candidate molecular targets for future mechanistic investigations into NOA-related male infertility.
ne0f87e4a3065: Teff (Eragrostis tef) occupies close to three million hectares of agricultural land in Ethiopia, nonetheless, realized yields remain substantially below the crop’s inherent genetic yield potential. Thus, this study aimed to examine how different sowing rates and methods impacted productivity of teff varieties in Mojana Wodera Woreda. The treatments included three varieties of teff (namely, Quncho, Kora and Abolse (local variety), three sowing rates (10, 15 and 20 kg ha −1), and three sowing methods (15 cm and 20 cm spacing between rows and broad casting). The interaction effect of seed rate, sowing method and variety significantly affected crop growth and yield parameters (P Quncho combined with 20 cm row spacing and at a seed rate of 10 kg ha–1. Quncho sown at a rate of 10 kg ha–1 with a row spacing of 15 cm produced the maximum amount of aboveground biomass yield (10.76 t ha–1). Furthermore, the highest lodging index (44%) was recorded when variety Quncho was sown with a broadcasting method at the highest seed rate of 20 kg ha–1. The main effect of seed rate, sowing method and variety significantly affected days to 50% heading (P Kora significantly took longer time (59.18) to reach 50% heading than variety Quncho and Abolse. Increasing row spacing to 20 cm prolong the time for 50% heading of teff varieties, while sowing teff variety at a a rate of 15 kg ha–1 also significantly increased the days to heading. Quncho produced the largest panicle length (45.14 cm) and yield (2.47 t ha–1) which is 15.96% higher than variety Kora and 26.67% higher than the grain yield obtained from the local Abolse variety. Furthermore, sowing teff at a row spacing of 20 cm produced the maximum panicle length (44.46 cm) and yield (2.32 t ha–1). As to the seed rate, thhe highest grain yield and largest panicle were when teff was seeded at 10 kg ha–1.
n42f3191e4091: by Xiaoqing Jiang Amid growing tourism pressure in communities surrounding major attractions, questions of governance legitimacy, fairness, and resident engagement have become increasingly salient. This study examines how residents’ perceptions of distributive, procedural, and interactional justice are associated with emotional solidarity with tourists and co-governance participation intention. Survey data from 308 residents living near major attractions in Wuxi, China, were analyzed using structural equation modeling, mediation analysis, and hierarchical regression analysis. The results show that all three dimensions of perceived justice are positively associated with emotional solidarity and co-governance participation intention, with procedural and interactional justice showing particularly strong associations. The mediation results indicate a significant indirect association between governance fairness and participation intention through emotional solidarity. The moderation results show that perceived tourism pressure is significant only for the association between interactional justice and emotional solidarity, while its moderating role is not significant for distributive or procedural justice. These findings suggest that residents’ willingness to engage in co-governance is associated not only with how tourism is managed institutionally, but also with their relational orientation toward tourists. The study highlights the importance of transparent procedures, meaningful resident voice, and respectful everyday interactions for understanding collaborative governance in urban destinations under sustained tourism pressure.
n3e6774984a1e: Background Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest remains a major public health concern, and early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) by bystanders is crucial for improving survival outcomes. University students represent an important target population for CPR education because they are socially active, highly accessible, and capable of disseminating lifesaving knowledge within the wider community. However, inadequate CPR knowledge, low willingness to perform CPR, and poor self-efficacy remain common among university students in Malaysia. Objectives This two-phase study aims to determine the prevalence of self-reported CPR-related knowledge, willingness, and self-efficacy among students in a Malaysian tertiary institution (Phase 1) and to explore the preliminary changes in these outcomes following a peer-led CPR workshop (Phase 2). Methods In Phase 1, a cross-sectional survey was conducted at a tertiary institute in Selangor, Malaysia using a validated questionnaire on knowledge, attitudes, behavioral intention, and self-efficacy (KABSE) (N = 431). In Phase 2, a two-hour peer-led workshop, delivered by medical students, targeted students without CPR training in the past two years, and pre–post KABSE changes were measured (N = 33). Results Phase 1 baseline findings revealed CPR knowledge and self-efficacy levels were relatively lower than attitudes and willingness to perform CPR. Females showed higher knowledge and attitudes, while males reported greater self-efficacy. Older and married participants demonstrated better attitudes, and those with a healthcare-related background had higher knowledge, attitudes, and self-efficacy, though similar behavioral intention. Higher scores were also linked to AED awareness, AED usage capability, and recent CPR training. Statistical analysis revealed significant associations among the KABSE domains. Following the peer-led workshop, the participants showed significant gains in self-reported knowledge (p < 0.001), attitude (p < 0.001), behavioral intention (p < 0.01), and self-efficacy (p < 0.001). Conclusion Although participants displayed positive attitudes toward CPR, baseline knowledge and self-efficacy were limited. The peer-led workshop demonstrated feasibility as a proof-of-concept intervention, generating significant short-term gains in self-reported knowledge and confidence.
n40ebe3d86763: Background Low peak expiratory flow (PEF) may precede the first self-report of recognized lung disease, but cross-cohort consistency and incremental value are uncertain. Methods We analysed Health and Retirement Study (HRS) discovery and prespecified person-disjoint replication samples and the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA). The estimand linked baseline PEF to the first subsequently observed self-report of recognized lung disease, not biological onset. HRS used a prespecified nominal lower-decile z score and ELSA an empirical lower decile. Participant-clustered models adjusted for demographic, clinical and functional factors. Weighting and a stroke comparator were sensitivity analyses. Post-hoc ELSA benchmarking compared PEF with FEV1 and FVC using person-disjoint cross-validation and full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity. Results Models included 18,510 HRS discovery windows (320 reports), 11,424 replication windows (188), and 8,634 ELSA person-waves (95). Low PEF was associated with first report in discovery (odds ratio [OR] 3.36, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.54–4.45), replication (3.14, 2.19–4.49), and ELSA (3.77, 2.36–6.01). Weighted estimates were similar; stroke associations were weaker or null. After adjustment for separate FEV1 and FVC indices, the continuous-PEF OR was 1.04 (0.90–1.20). In 1,584 fixed-horizon participants (95 events), AUCs were 0.650 for covariates, 0.684 with PEF, 0.745 with FEV1 and FVC, and 0.739 with all three. Full-pipeline bootstrap sensitivity found no clear incremental evidence beyond FEV1 and FVC. Across differing horizons, low-PEF rules identified fewer than one-third of reports in HRS replication and ELSA. Conclusions Lower PEF was associated with a subsequent first observed lung-disease report; cohort-specific low-PEF rules identified fewer than one-third. In exploratory fixed out-of-fold predictions, PEF improved average precision and prediction error over covariates; no clear incremental evidence remained after FEV1 and FVC. Same-protocol collection does not establish a peak-flow-only pathway.
n02b81fa7e302: Acid affected soils have been expanding in the Ethiopian highlands, and caused serious yield decline. Organic amendments and lime have been used to manage soil acidity. However, the rate and the right combinations have not been sufficiently documented for various crops and locations. This study aimed at investigating the effects of four manure rates (0, 4, 8, and 12 t ha-1), with three lime rates (0, 1.5 and 3 t ha-1 CaCO3) on maize yield, and selected soil chemical properties. The experiment was arranged in factorial combinations using randomized complete block design (RCBD) with three replications. The result showed that significant variations were obtained for yield, and yield components of maize where maximum grain yield (4087.0 kg ha-1) was harvested from the combination of 8 t manure ha-1 with 1.5 t lime ha-1. However, significantly (P < 0.01) highest stalk yield (11155.0 kg ha-1) and yield of dry aboveground biomass (14803.7 kg ha-1) were achieved from the integrations of 3 t lime with 12 t manure ha-1. The plots that received 12 t ha-1 manure only had the highest OC content (1.96%), with an increase of 54%. Following 3 t ha-1 lime plus 12 t ha-1 manure applications, the available P content was found to be significantly (P < 0.01) the highest (14.41 mg kg-1). The present experiment indicated that integrated application of 3 t ha-1 lime with 8 t ha-1 manure could help increase maize yield and profitability while maintaining fertility of soils in acid affected soils of Meket area and similar other locations.
nd3eb1f70bafd: Introduction Menstrual health is a critical yet neglected public health issue among tribal adolescent girls in India, influenced by socio-cultural, economic, and infrastructural determinants. This review aimed to explore the key menstrual health challenges, barriers, and associated outcomes among tribal adolescent girls in India. Methods This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2015 and March 2026. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies focusing on menstrual health among tribal adolescent girls in India were included. Study selection, data extraction, and quality appraisal were conducted independently by multiple reviewers. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) tools. Due to heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis approach was adopted. Results Out of 197 identified records, 28 studies met the inclusion criteria. The findings reveal significant disparities in menstrual health management driven by socioeconomic status, education, cultural taboos, and infrastructural limitations. Key challenges included limited access to sanitary products, inadequate WASH facilities, and poor awareness. Cultural stigma and restrictive practices contributed to psychological distress and unsafe hygiene behaviours. These barriers were associated with adverse outcomes such as reproductive tract infections and increased school absenteeism. The quality appraisal indicated overall moderate to high methodological rigour, with most studies demonstrating acceptable quality despite some limitations related to study design and reporting. Conclusion Menstrual health among tribal adolescent girls remains a significant public health concern in India. Addressing these challenges requires integrated, culturally sensitive interventions focusing on education, improved infrastructure, and equitable access to menstrual health services to enhance health outcomes and well-being.
n9dfc0faf16ac: The current study addresses increasing global problems (agricultural sustainability, environmental contamination, and antimicrobial resistance) by means of sustainable and multifunctional biosynthesized Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). The study utilized a cell-free supernatant of a novel endophytic bacterial strain (Niallia Circulans) to synthesize ZnO NPs. Biosynthesized NPs were evaluated by using various techniques of characterization. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) was revealed by UV-Visible spectral peak for ZnO NPs at 355 nm. A X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed a crystallite size of 90.64 nm, while scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDX) demonstrated the predominance of hexagonal-structured zinc, carbon, and oxygen elements. The functional groups in Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) confirm the presence of biomolecules. The evaluated multifunctional application of biosynthesized ZnO NPs exhibits an enhanced early seedling growth rate and increased seed germination (100% in 12 h) on cowpea (Vigna unguiculata L.) compared to the control groups. Also shows excellent antibacterial activity against test bacterial strains. Additionally, a high removal efficiency of 97.85% was achieved within 110 min for 10 ppm methylene blue dye solution at pH 9. This study highlights the endophytic bacteria-mediated successful synthesis of ZnO NPs, with potential multifunctional applications in agriculture, antimicrobial treatments, and environmental remediation.
n007584522aa7: SARS-CoV-2 infection is linked to hematologic abnormalities, but whether early hematopoietic compartments and their stromal niche are directly engaged remains unclear. We used in vitro exposure models to compare variant-associated responses of adult mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and umbilical cord blood (UCB) CD34 ⁺ hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). Adipose–derived (AD) and bone marrow–derived (BM) MSCs exposed to wild-type, Delta, or Omicron showed source- and variant-dependent nucleocapsid protein (NP) positivity, highest with Omicron in AD-MSCs; infectious virus in supernatants was undetectable. AD-MSCs expressed higher neuropilin-1 (NRP1) than BM-MSCs, and NRP1 knockdown reduced Omicron-associated NP signal, implicating an NRP1-linked entry process. SARS-CoV-2 exposure induced indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 (IDO1), most prominently in AD-MSCs. In UCB CD34 ⁺ HSPCs, Omicron increased NP positivity enriched in long-term HSCs, reduced primitive fraction frequencies, increased colony formation, and promoted early erythroid progenitor accumulation; heat-inactivated virus did not. NanoString profiling revealed host-response activation and altered cell-cycle/differentiation programs. These data indicate Omicron can engage stromal and early hematopoietic compartments and remodel stress-responsive hematopoiesis.
n31f0997b5dad: The incidence of low birthweight (LBiW) piglets, which show impaired growth compared to normal birthweight (NBiW) littermates, has increased with litter size. We previously reported that glutamine increased the bodyweight and plasma glutamine concentrations in LBiW piglets, with no effect on jejunal glutamine concentrations or glutamine transport and metabolism mRNA abundance. In this study, we investigated the effect of glutamine supplementation on proteinogenic free amino acid (FAA), protein-bound AA (PBAA) and AA-metabolite profiles, mRNA abundance, fractional protein synthesis (FPSR) and the plasma metabolome. At birth (0 days of age (d)), 24 pairs of male LBiW (1.10 kg ± 0.02) and NBiW (1.50 kg ± 0.02) littermates were selected. At 1 d, litters were standardized to 12 piglets, and piglets supplemented daily with either glutamine (1 g/kg bodyweight) or isonitrogenous amounts of alanine (1.22 g/kg bodyweight), until 5 d. Stomach content FAA, AA-metabolites, duodenal and liver tissue FAA, PBAA, AA-metabolites, biochemical indices, duodenal, colon and liver tissue FPSR, liver tissue and duodenal mucosa glutamine transport and metabolism mRNA abundance and the plasma metabolome were analysed. Stomach digesta glutamine (P P = 0.02; NBiW, P = 0.03) concentrations were higher in glutamine than alanine piglets. Analysis by Data Integration Analysis for Biomarker Discovery using Latent Variable Approaches for Omics Studies showed glutamine, carnosine, citrulline and alanine separated the supplementation groups, whilst glutathione reductase, glutathione synthetase and tight junction protein 1 mRNA separated glutamine LBiW piglets from alanine. Duodenal RNA was lower and Protein-to-RNA ratio higher (P = 0.004) in glutamine than alanine LBiW piglets (P = 0.02). Colon FPSR was higher in NBiW than LBiW piglets supplemented with Ala. No effects on the plasma metabolome were observed. These results show that not all glutamine passed through the stomach, and that glutamine is absorbed and metabolised in the duodenum, potentially altering the intracellular pH, and appears to increase oxidative stress markers in the duodenum of LBiW piglets.
n7f2471e35194: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, immune dysregulation, and metabolic imbalance. To define lipid metabolism-related transcriptional heterogeneity within the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP)/synovium compartment, we integrated publicly available single-cell transcriptomic data from IPFP/synovium-derived joint cells with bulk synovial transcriptomic datasets from patients with KOA and controls. Lipid metabolism-related scores were derived using multiple single-cell scoring algorithms, and candidate genes were identified through score-associated analyses, differential expression, protein–protein interaction analysis, and five machine-learning approaches, followed by external bulk validation and single-cell characterization. Myeloid cells showed the most consistent KOA-associated increases in lipid metabolism-related transcriptional scores. Fifty composite-score-associated genes were identified and were enriched in lipid metabolic, lysosomal, and PPAR-related pathways. Cross-screening prioritized PLIN2, LTA4H, and PPT1, with LTA4H showing the strongest association with lipid metabolism-related transcriptional scores. LTA4H was predominantly enriched in myeloid cells, particularly monocytes and inflammatory macrophages, and was increased in KOA myeloid cells and high-score cells. Cell–cell communication, myeloid subclustering, and pseudotime analyses linked LTA4H-positive myeloid cells to inflammatory signaling and the transition from monocytes toward inflammatory macrophages. In silico knockout analysis further implicated LTA4H in regulatory programs related to leukocyte migration, chemotaxis, phagocytosis, and cytokine receptor binding. In a rat KOA model, LTA4H protein expression was increased in knee synovial tissues and spatially colocalized with CD68-positive macrophages. These findings define a myeloid-cell-centered context for LTA4H in KOA and link its expression to lipid metabolism-related transcriptional features and inflammatory myeloid-cell states.
n3a2f5b83c9f3: Background Odontogenic infections may progress to life-threatening complications if not managed promptly, and socioeconomic circumstances have been linked to their presentation, particularly where access to dental care is limited. Because every patient studied was already hospitalised, this analysis addresses the clinical type of infection at presentation, not the risk of developing one. Methodology A retrospective cross-sectional review of hospital records was undertaken at the Allied Ward of Sunyani Teaching Hospital (January 2021 to January 2025). Of 811 consecutive admissions, 525 were excluded: 509 for non-odontogenic conditions and 16 for records missing more than 30% of required clinical fields, leaving 286 complete records. Chi-square tests were reported with Cramer’s V and Monte Carlo exact p-values where cells were sparse. Because the unpenalised model showed quasi-complete separation, the primary analysis was a Firth-penalised multinomial logistic regression, with abscess as the reference outcome. Results Adjusting for age, sex, employment, residence, recorded oral hygiene, systemic comorbidity and alcohol use, unemployment was associated with higher adjusted odds of Ludwig’s angina (LA) and not abscess (AOR = 2.78, 95% CI 1.27–6.09), and rural residence with necrotizing fasciitis (NF; AOR = 3.62, 95% CI 1.33–9.80). Systemic comorbidity was associated with LA (AOR = 4.14, 95% CI 1.83–9.36), NF (AOR = 8.72, 95% CI 2.95–25.75) and cellulitis (AOR = 2.07, 95% CI 1.03–4.18). Absence of a recorded poor-hygiene entry was associated with cellulitis (AOR = 8.05, 95% CI 2.42–26.83), interpreted as a documentation artefact not a protective effect. Sex and alcohol use showed no association. Number of children, the sole source of separation, was not retained; its penalised intervals included 1. Conclusion Unemployment and systemic comorbidity were associated with more severe presentations, and rural residence with NF specifically. Findings are associational and describe variation in infection type among admitted patients rather than infection risk, within a retrospective single-centre design.
nae6f28c065a3: Temporal Action Localization (TAL) aims to identify all action categories along with their precise temporal boundaries in untrimmed videos. It serves as a fundamental task supporting various downstream applications, including intelligent video editing, automatic summarization, anomaly detection, and human–computer interaction. Despite significant progress, TAL in real-world scenarios remains challenging due to two critical factors: substantial intra-class variations in action duration, ranging from a few seconds to several minutes, and severe degradation of boundary localization accuracy caused by variations in illumination, background clutter, and camera viewpoints. To address these issues, this paper presents a Temporal Action Localization with Class-Guided Boundary Regression (TAL-CGBR) framework, which incorporates semantic information from the classification branch into the regression network to enhance boundary precision. In addition, a window-based attention mechanism and a temporal hierarchical feature structure are introduced to improve computational efficiency while maintaining high localization accuracy. Experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed TAL-CGBR achieves competitive performance, attaining 68.5% average mAP on THUMOS14 and 36.7% average mAP on ActivityNet v1.3, ranking second among recent methods and demonstrating a favorable balance between accuracy and computational efficiency.
n6ab160ebe532: Background The current study investigated host genetic associations with disease severity in COVID-19 patients of South Asian origin and explored its molecular basis. Methods Covid-19 patients were stratified into disease severity groups based on the clinical and radiographic findings. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood samples. A two-step discovery and validation approach was utilized for genetic analysis. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) based variant prioritization was performed in a discovery cohort of severe disease patients followed by validation in an independent cohort. Bioinformatics analysis including data alignment, and annotation to the GRCh38 human reference genome was done by Ensembl VEP software. WES filtration pipeline utilizing predicted pathogenicity and population allele frequencies focused on the low-frequency and rare variants to filter out the variants of concern. Computational predictive tools and simulations were utilized for the structural and functional analysis of the identified high-risk SNP. Statistical analyses were done by SPSS version 24 and GraphPad Prism version 10. Results The missense variant rs199726033 of SVIL gene demonstrated the highest recurrence in the WES discovery cohort. The minor allele frequency (29.2%) was substantially higher than that reported for South Asians in the gnomAD v4 database (1.051%). A significant association of the mutant AC genotype of rs199726033 and disease severity was found in the validation cohort. Protein modeling and structural analysis localized the variant within a functionally conserved Gelsolin domain. Moreover, functional and pathway analysis of the SVIL variant indicates its potential role in actin filament remodeling relevant to COVID-19 related vasculopathy and cytoskeleton dynamics thus influencing host-viral interactions. Conclusion A SVIL missense variant is associated with disease severity and may influence host cytoskeletal processes relevant to COVID-19 severity.
n205fc5251097: CRISPR/Cas9-induced DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are widely used for genome engineering, yet their capacity to provoke sister chromatid exchange (SCE) remains incompletely understood because exchanges between identical sisters leave no sequence change and are invisible to conventional sequencing. Using sci-L3-Strand-seq, a scalable single-cell template-strand sequencing platform, we mapped SCE following targeted Cas9 cleavage. Cas9 targeting of a unique genomic locus strongly enriched SCE at the break site, reaching 41% in the same cell cycle and 17% in the subsequent division, indicating frequent non-local inter-sister repair. Targeting 237 repetitive Alu sites produced mild enrichment of on-target SCE, whereas cells with elevated SCE burden showed significant enrichment at programmed cut sites, suggesting context-dependent recombination at repetitive loci. Reciprocal daughter-cell pair analysis revealed large-scale structural alterations on chromosomes with induced SCEs and at SCE junctions, indicating that Cas9-induced SCE does not universally reflect error-free homologous recombination. Disruption of LIG3, LIG4, XRCC1, and XRCC4 at Cas9 cut sites did not measurably alter SCE frequency, consistent with delayed functional loss following editing. Together, these findings identify Cas9-induced DSBs as potent local triggers of SCE and reveal structural outcomes invisible to conventional sequencing.
ne1edffd4d992: Accurate prediction of ligand-bound protein complexes and ranking them by affinity are central problems in drug discovery. While deep-learning co-folding methods can help address these challenges, their evaluation has been hampered by the difficulties in assessing independence from training data and insufficiently large test sets. Here, we test the ability of co-folding methods to predict the structures of 551 ligands, 489 of which are of sufficient quality for evaluation, bound to the SARS-CoV-2 NSP3 macrodomain (Mac1) that were determined after the training cutoff dates. AlphaFold3 (AF3), Boltz-2, and Chai-1 each reproduced >50% of the Mac1 ligand poses to better than 2 Å root-mean-square deviation of experiment. Despite the potential for co-folding to describe protein conformational changes that stabilize ligand binding, we did not find that common conformational rearrangements, including peptide flip and a large loop opening, were recapitulated by the co-folding prediction. For AF3 and Chai-1, ligand pose prediction confidence weakly, but significantly, tracked experimental potency, while DOCK3.7 energies were only weakly correlated. Boltz-2 affinity predictions showed the strongest correlation with measured potency and, after calibration, achieved lower mean absolute error than a baseline predictor. We next assessed whether co-folding scores could rescore docking hit lists to distinguish true ligands from non-binders among hundreds of molecules prospectively experimentally tested against AmpC β-lactamase, the dopamine D4, and the σ2 receptors. AF3 ligand pose confidence values did not separate true ligands from high-scoring false positives as effectively as docking scores or Boltz-2 affinity predictions did. Taken together, the modest, but independent correlations of docking score and co-folding confidence or affinity suggest that integrating physics-based and deep-learning approaches may help with hit prioritization and subsequent optimization in structure-based ligand discovery.
n86f0ab86a2bd: To maintain metabolic homeostasis, enzymes must adapt to fluctuating nutrient levels through mechanisms beyond gene expression. Here, we demonstrate that human glutamine synthetase (GS) can reversibly polymerize into filaments aided by a composite binding site formed at the filament interface by the product, glutamine. Time-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) confirms that glutamine binding stabilizes these filaments, which in turn exhibit reduced catalytic specificity for ammonia at physiological concentrations. This inhibition appears induced by a conformational change that remodulates the active site loop ensemble gating substrate entry. Metadynamics ensemble refinement revealed >10 Å conformational range for the active site loop and that the loop is stabilized by transient contacts. This disorder is significant, as we show that the transient contacts which stabilize this loop in a closed conformation are essential for catalysis both in vitro and in cells. We propose that GS filament formation constitutes a negative-feedback mechanism, directly linking product concentration to the structural and functional remodeling of the enzyme.
n37ff1662716b: Non-invasive recordings of brain electrophysiology provide credible insights into decline in neuronal functioning with age. New approaches are required to translate these results into compelling clinical metrics and meet the global challenge of preserving brain health in ageing. Changes in neuronal dynamics with ageing are observable in the power spectra of EEG and MEG recordings. Highly promising candidates for electrophysiological markers have been identified, but progress is hindered by substantial methodological variability across studies. This makes it challenging to establish a clear consensus on the frequency, location, and direction of any single reported effect within the larger body of research. We estimate a full-frequency whole-head profile of the ageing effect on eyes-closed resting-state MEG using the GLM-Spectrum. This data representation is easily sharable, facilitates meta-analyses, and provides a framework for estimating statistical power of age effects for future study planning. We use this to show that the effect of age replicates across open-access MEG datasets and is robust to modelling of common covariates. Distinct components within the full-frequency profile have different effect sizes, indicating that sample-size planning for ageing effects must consider the specific features of interest. The frequency profile of ageing is strongly robust to a range of common covariates and partially robust to modelling of grey matter volume. We establish that what seems a well-powered study may become underpowered when analyses target an age effect that is linearly separable from an age-relevant covariate such as grey matter volume. These results provide a pathway towards formal comparison and assessment of candidate markers for brain health in ageing.
n7231b13876c8: Disruptions in airway branching or alveolar differentiation during lung development can lead to severe respiratory deficiencies and neonatal death. The molecular mechanisms governing branching patterning and early alveolar formation remain elusive. Loss of Svep1 function in mice results in various developmental defects, including lung hypoplasia and perinatal lethality. Our examination of the lungs of Svep1 knockout (Svep1-/-) mouse embryos, both in vivo and in vitro, revealed that Svep1 mutants exhibit an increase in the number of disorganized distal airway tips, progressively greater disruption of lung lobe morphology over time, and disrupted saccular development. Svep1 interacts with FGF signaling to regulate smooth muscle differentiation and, together with Fgf9, guides airway branching patterning. Transcriptomic data from the lungs of Svep1-/- embryos revealed dysregulated gene expression affecting saccular maturation. Our findings demonstrate that Svep1 is a key extracellular matrix player shaping airway morphology and influencing alveolar fate. These insights offer potential avenues for therapeutic interventions in congenital lung disorders.
nbabf98f320c0: Hormones mediate inter-organ signaling, which is crucial in orchestrating diverse behaviors and physiological processes, including sleep and activity, feeding, growth, metabolism, and reproduction. The pars intercerebralis and pars lateralis in insects represent major hubs that contain neurosecretory cells (NSCs) that produce various peptide hormones. To obtain insight into how hormonal signaling is regulated, we have characterized the synaptic connectome of NSCs in the adult Drosophila brain. Identification of neurons providing inputs to multiple NSC classes implicates diuretic hormone 44-expressing NSCs as a major coordinator of physiology and behavior. Surprisingly, despite most NSCs having dendrites in the subesophageal zone (primary taste processing center), inputs from peripheral gustatory neurons to NSCs are largely indirect. We also deciphered pathways via which diverse olfactory inputs are relayed to NSCs. Using an influence metric, based on a linear dynamical systems approach, we identify enteric neurons as the strongest influencers of NSC activity compared to other sensory modalities. Further, our analyses revealed substantial inputs from brain descending neurons to NSCs, suggesting that descending neurons regulate both endocrine and motor output to synchronize physiological changes with appropriate behaviors. In contrast to NSC inputs, synaptic output from NSCs is sparse and mostly mediated by corazonin NSCs. We show that both corazonin-expressing NSCs and their downstream synaptic partner DNg27 influence egg-laying. We additionally explore putative paracrine interconnectivity between NSC classes and peptide hormone pathways from NSCs to peripheral tissues by analyzing single-cell transcriptomic datasets. Our comprehensive characterization of the Drosophila neurosecretory network connectome provides a platform to understand complex hormonal networks and how they orchestrate animal behaviors and physiology.
nde82a753ca1c: Synaptic depression is often interpreted as reflecting depletion of the readily releasable pool (RRP) following exocytosis. Such a mechanism predicts little or no depression at low stimulation frequency, as RRP replenishment should then offset the loss of vesicles by exocytosis. Nevertheless, in several types of mammalian central synapses, repetitive presynaptic stimulation at low frequency (<5 Hz) elicits synaptic depression (low-frequency depression or LFD). In the present work, we count the number of synaptic vesicles released at individual active zones to study the RRP and its replenishment during LFD. Contrary to depletion models of synaptic depression, we find that LFD does not depend on previous SV consumption. We find that LFD displays a long recovery time course (tens of seconds) when challenged by isolated stimulations but is immediately reversed by a high-frequency train. We suggest that LFD results from undocking, a shift between two classes of synaptic vesicles organized sequentially inside the RRP (replacement vs. docked vesicles) in favor of the upstream (replacement) state. To explain the dependence of LFD recovery on stimulation frequency, we propose that, while undocking is apparent hundreds of milliseconds after a stimulation, calcium-dependent docking takes only a couple of milliseconds. Consistent with the undocking model, we find that double presynaptic stimulations alleviate LFD as they favor vesicular docking and RRP replenishment. Finally, we expand our model to explain how stimulation frequency shapes short-term synaptic depression, changing from depression at low frequency to a facilitation-depression sequence at medium- or high-frequency trains.
n7fe19a193cc8: In team-sports, agility, perceptual-cognitive abilities, and executive functions are crucial for performance and injury prevention. Incorporating motor-cognitive demands into neuromuscular warm-ups may improve coping with cognitively demanding movement situations, requiring time-constrained decision-making and reactive responses. This randomized three-arm crossover study investigated the acute effects of the Prevent Injury and Enhance Performance (PEP) warm-up and two adapted motor-cognitive versions (PEP+; PEP-SKILLCOURT) on pre-planned (n = 6) and unplanned countermovement jump-landings, with the landing side cued only after take-off (n = 16). Eighteen team-sport athletes (age: 23 ± 3 years; height: 181 ± 11.4 cm; weight: 75.6 ± 10.4 kg; 5 females) completed the three warm-ups on separate days. PEP+ included cognitive exercises targeting visuomotor processing and executive functions. PEP-SKILLCOURT incorporated reactive agility exercises using the SKILLCOURT device. After each warm-up, participants performed the jump-landing task on a capacitive pressure plate. Landing performance was assessed using biomechanical and error-related outcomes, including peak vertical ground reaction force (pVGRF), time to pVGRF, center of pressure path length (CoP), time to stabilization (TTS), standing errors, and decision errors. Linear and generalized mixed models were used to analyze biomechanical outcomes and error counts, respectively, adjusting for flight time. No significant carryover effects occurred (p > .05). Landing condition significantly affected pVGRF and CoP (−4 to +17%, p = .003–.004) as well as error rates (p = .002). Post hoc tests indicated lower pVGRF, greater CoP fluctuations (p = .041 to <.001), and more errors (p = .037 to <.001) during unplanned landings. After Holm adjustment, no significant treatment or treatment × landing condition interaction effects remained. However, exploratory trends suggested lower landing loads and reduced CoP fluctuations after PEP+. Unplanned conditions resulted in poorer landing control and more erroneous landings, indicating reduced task performance. Larger trials are needed to confirm the exploratory trends favoring PEP+ and examine joint-specific biomechanics relevant to injury risk.
nc095a12bc7a8: The Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging zoonotic orthobunyavirus responsible for recurring outbreaks of febrile illness and neurological disorders in South and Central America. Despite its growing public health issues, no FDA-approved vaccines or antiviral therapies currently exist. To address this gap, a multiepitope subunit vaccine was designed to target OROV glycoproteins G1 (Gn), G2 (Gc), and the nucleocapsid (N) protein using a reverse-vaccinology (RV) approach. For vaccine construction, suitable epitopes (MHC-I, MHC-II, and linear B-cell) were selected based on percentile rank, antigenicity, allergenicity, and toxicity. However, the biophysical attributes demonstrated advantageous characteristics, including stability and solubility (GRAVY score: −0.432). The structural modelling exhibited a Ramachandran and Z scores of 91.86% (most favoured regions) and −1.81, respectively. However, the molecular docking with TLR-2 and TLR-4 receptors showed probable interactions (−1126.8 kJ/mol) and (−1239.4 kJ/mol), respectively. Moreover, dynamics simulation of the vaccine and Vaccine-TLR-4 complexes confirmed probable dynamic stability and compactness. The codon optimisation for Escherichia coli K12 expression yielded a CAI value of 1.0 and a GC content of (30–70) %, indicating optimal expression. The immune simulation predicted strong antibody-mediated and T cell-mediated immunity, including elevated IFN-γ, IgG, and memory cell populations. These findings suggest the potential of multiepitope subunit vaccines as a promising preventive candidate against OROV. However, additional experimental verification is required to confirm its immunogenicity and safety in experimental settings.
ncc489538aaeb: Accurate assessment of urban patrol cases plays an important role in maintaining urban safety and improving the efficiency of urban governance. The hazard level of urban patrol cases can be reflected by the urgency level and prioritizing high-urgency cases can help reduce potential risks to public safety. However, it remains challenging to assess the urgency level of urban patrol cases when reliable urgency labels are limited or unavailable. To address this problem, this paper proposes an urban patrol case urgency classification method based on self-supervised clustering of a graph neural network. First, a case-relationship graph is constructed from urban patrol cases. A graph attention-based autoencoder is then pretrained to learn node representations, and K-means is used to initialize cluster centers. Finally, representation learning and clustering are jointly optimized to identify urgency-oriented clusters without using manual labels during training. Experimental validation was conducted using 6126 urban patrol case records from Zhengzhou, China. The proposed method achieved a Recall of 0.7458, Precision of 0.7465, ACC of 0.7424, F1 of 0.7403, and NMI of 0.4517. Compared with TADW, the strongest baseline, the proposed method improved these metrics by 0.0617, 0.0479, 0.0650, 0.0690, and 0.0407, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively learn urgency-related latent representations and improve the classification quality of urban patrol cases.
n22c1c8b72f77: Objective To analyze the distribution and epidemiological characteristics of critical illnesses in the emergency department of Hebei Children's Hospital. Method Through retrospective medical record review, patients triaged as level Ⅰ or Ⅱ (aged 0–18 years) who visited the emergency department of the hospital from January 2023 to December 2024 were included. The distribution of diseases, age, gender, season and other indicators were statistically analyzed. Results A total of 1,450 critically ill patients with triage levels Ⅰ and Ⅱ were included. The median (IQR) age of all patients was 4.00 (1.00, 9.00) years, and the male-to-female ratio was 1.2:1. Among each age group, the 1 to <3 years group had a proportion of 27.9%, and the 0 to <1 year group had a proportion of 9.5%, representing the highest and lowest values, respectively. The distribution of critical illnesses in the emergency department of this hospital was led by the nervous system (n = 548, 37.8%), trauma and accidental injuries (n = 286, 19.7%), and the respiratory system (n = 214, 14.8%), which ranked as the top three categories. The top five primary diagnosed diseases were seizure (n = 352, 24.3%), drug poisoning (n = 242, 16.7%), severe pneumonia (n = 137, 9.5%), status epileptics (n = 137, 9.5%), and arrhythmia (n = 102, 7.0%). Among them, the proportion of severe pneumonia was the highest in the 0 to <1 year group; the proportion of seizure was the highest in the 1 to <3 years group, 3 to <6 years group and 6 to <12 years group, while the proportion of drug poisoning was the highest in the 12 to <18 years group. The distribution of the top five disease differed significantly across age groups (p < 0.001) and seasons (p = 0.004). Cardiopulmonary arrest (CPA) is one of the most critical conditions in an emergency department. However, the distribution of diseases causing CPA did not show significant differences by age or season. The top three diseases causing CPA are severe pneumonia, asphyxia, and multiple body region injuries (Road traffic accident). Conclusion The spectrum of critical illnesses varied significantly by age and seasonal distribution in the emergency department of Hebei Children's Hospital. Therefore, age and season-tailored approaches are recommended for managing common critical illnesses, whereas CPA requires a standardized, universally applied emergency response. It is necessary to further strengthen training and optimize resource allocation.
naaf928c88978: Purpose This study aimed to implement a previously developed quality indicator system for pharmaceutical care in orthopedic perioperative pain management and evaluate its impact on adherence to pharmaceutical care standards. Methods A single-center before-and-after study with a historical control was conducted in 200 patients scheduled for elective orthopedic surgery. A retrospective pre-intervention cohort (n = 100, Nov 2024–Jan 2025) was evaluated to establish a reference, followed by targeted interventions. A prospective post-intervention cohort (n = 100, Apr–Jun 2025) was then evaluated. Groups were compared on overall adherence (Ci ≥ 0.6) to pharmaceutical care standards and full-score attainment rates of quality indicators. A sensitivity analysis was performed to assess the impact of documentation bias. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Results Overall adherence increased from 41% to 91% (risk difference, 50 percentage points; 95% CI, 37.83–60.05; P P P > 0.05). Among the other 15 process and outcome indicators, 13 remained significant after Bonferroni correction (α = 0.0031), with risk differences ranging from 14 to 33 percentage points. Sensitivity analysis supported the robustness of the finding. Improvements were observed across structural (descriptive), process, and outcome indicators, with the majority of process and outcome indicators showing significant gains after conservative correction.
